column5: READ LIVE 2026-09-21 with get_metadata, node by node, for the one item this row has carried as unread since wave 50 - the phone seam between the board and the panel - and it is 8, the same seam the desktop cut draws. Inside `Frame 271` 9691:11954 (375 x 851) the board `Mobile` 9799:14905 is 375 x 475 at y=0 and the panel 9691:12046 is 375 x 368 at y=483, so 475 + 8 + 368 = 851, the block's own height, exactly as 356 + 8 + 954 = 1318 closes on the desktop block. BUILT (skai-gaming 2d8a3837): the route row was `flex gap-4` with an `lg:gap-2` ramp, which drew twice the frame's seam on every width below lg; it is now a flat gap-2 on the route arm and the ramp is gone, because a ramp is a claim that the two cuts disagree and they do not. Bingo draws NO 768 board - bingo.titles.tsv carries the 1440 and the 375 cut and no tablet one - so the still-stacked rung between md and lg inherits the phone cut, stated as an inheritance rather than a measurement. The dialog arm keeps its own 16 and now carries it on its own literal: DialogContent is a fixed 1024 box transformed to fit, so a viewport-keyed seam fires at the wrong times inside it and no frame draws the dialog. bingoGameRowSeam.test.ts was corrected with the code - its docblock asserted that the desktop 8 was 'the only seam that has been read' and pinned the stacked cut at 16 on that basis, which this reading overturns - and its arms are now extracted from the one ternary that carries them, pinned to a unique match that throws on 0 or 2+. ★ WHAT THIS PASS ADDS FOR THE ONE REMAINING ITEM, measured off the same dump at no extra read: the page column's three block heights are NOT free-floating content, they decompose exactly. More games `Main container` 11894:18433 is 343 x 254 at (16,1577) = heading Frame 345 343 x 36 + an 8 gap + row 11894:18444 at y=44 x 210. Bets 11894:18541 is 343 x 204 at (16,1855) = heading 343 x 24 + an 8 gap + Frame 279 at y=32 x 172. About/FAQ Frame 642 11894:18590 is 343 x 1097 at (16,2107) = content 343 x 653 + a 24 gap + FAQ 343 x 420 at y=677, under a rule at y=2083. The heights STILL are not closed: those three blocks are drawn by the shared PlayGameDetailSections for every routed game, so checking them is checking a shared surface against one board, and no browser ran. READ LIVE 2026-09-21 with get_metadata, whole node, as the third independent reading of this cut - and it OVERTURNS the divergence that has kept the row open. 954 x 621, exactly TWO children and no hidden sibling: the row `Frame 1000004029` 9204:17801 at (181, 217.18359), 595.1658325 x 112.63317, five tiles of 112.63317 on a 120.63317 pitch each holding a 70 face at a 21.31658 inset and an ordinal row 98 x 18 at y 6.8164 whose 9 x 18 numeral sits at x=89 beside a 15 x 15 chip at x=0; and the footer 9204:17727 884 x 90 at (35,511) with Frame 464 and Frame 466 each 425 x 66 at x=12 and x=447 on a 10 gutter. Every one of those closes against the widget. ★★ THE PLACEMENT IS THE FRAME'S OWN STALE CENTRING, PROVEN RATHER THAN ARGUED. Two waves recorded x=181 as an unexplained 1.58 off centre and declined to build it. 181 is EXACTLY (954 - 592) / 2, and 592 is five 112 tiles on four 8 gaps - the row before its tiles each grew 0.63317. The residual proves it to float noise: 181 - (954 - 595.1658)/2 = 1.5829162 and 5 x 0.63317 / 2 = 1.5829277. So the board CENTRES this row and its absolute x was never re-centred after the children grew; the widget centres it, which is the board's intent, and no code change is owed. The y is the same family: 217.18359 is exact centring of the CURRENT row in a 547-tall region (2y + 112.63317 = 547.0004) and sits exactly 18.000 below a centring above the footer, and nothing on the board is 547 or 74. On a node whose every dimension is fractional because the whole widget is drawn at 0.8333x - 112.63317, 595.16583, 21.31658, 6.8164 - a round 18.000000 is an artefact of a hand-nudge, not a drawn value; building a literal 217 would also break at every other height, since the desktop board takes its height from the panel. BUILT (skai-gaming d392e2d9): the one number that WAS short, max-w-[595px] against the frame's 595.1658, is now the frame's. It is not cosmetic - every tile dimension in this file is a ratio of the container's inline size, so the 0.1658 came off the tile too and made it 112.60 where the file's own docblock claims 112.6332. ⛔ NOT MINE AND NOT TOUCHED: coinflipOdds.test.ts is RED at HEAD and it is a MONEY mismatch, not parity - cb1a6107 took COIN_MULTIPLIER to 1.9 for the 95% retune while the chain's settleCoinFlip still pays 19500/10000 = 1.95, so the UI quotes a figure the deployed rail does not pay. Never a lane fix. No browser ran.

READ LIVE 2026-09-21 with get_metadata, node by node, and BUILT (skai-gaming 35609ff5) - which is the first build this row has ever carried, because it was parked. ★★ THE HOLD WAS WRONG. The row read 'NOT BUILT: HELD BY RULING 0f0df6da - this is the Target grid', and that ruling (Casey 2026-09-14, the Game Mode row hidden so Target is unreachable) was SUPERSEDED THE NEXT DAY. CoinFlipGame.tsx:1697-1704 records it: Casey's 2026-09-15 ruling gave Target a chain model, so the same switch opens it, and at HEAD `targetPlayable = variants.coinflipTarget && currency !== "POINTS"` (:1109) - a live keeper variant parsed from `coinflip_target === true` in services/gaming/gameVariants.ts:33, whose GAME_VARIANTS_CLOSED is only the fallback. So nothing in code freezes Target and no ruling removes this frame's element; the board governs. THE NUMBERS: frame 375 x 347. Grid `Frame 1000004029` 9206:19964 is 316 x 252 at (30.0002, 12), four rows of five 60 x 60 tiles at 0/64/128/192/256 on a 4 gutter (row pitch 64), closing on 316, each holding a 42.7564 face at an 8.6473 inset. Footer 9206:19911 343 x 58 at (16, 277): pad 6, gutter 6, two 162.5 x 46 fields at x=6 and x=174.5, each a 41 x 14 label over a 162.5 x 30 card whose signals inset 8. WHAT CLOSED: the grid is a FIXED 316 CENTRED, not an inset - 29.5 on the Auto twin is exactly (375 - 316) / 2 - and the file drew it `w-full max-w-[595px]`, about 359 on a 375 board, cutting a 68 tile where both cuts draw 60. It is now max-w-[316px] lg:max-w-[595.1658px], pinned by the new coinflipTileGridWidth.test.ts. The footer already matched and is re-verified at source: w-[calc(100%-8px)] off a 351 content box = 343, gap-[6px] p-[6px], field 46 = a 10/14 label + a 2 gap + a 30 card with px-2 at 12/14. The grid's y=12 is the card's own p-3. STILL OPEN, both measured here: (1) the board floor is max-lg:min-h-[357px], the CLASSIC cut's height, where this cut and its Auto twin both draw 347 - one element, three cuts, and the floor is the max so nothing clips, so following 347 means keying the floor to `layout`, which is a call about the board rather than this grid; (2) one gap ratio serves both boards and they no longer agree - TILE_RATIO.gap is the desktop 8/112.6332 = 0.0710 against these cuts' 4/60 = 0.0667, so the tile lands 59.80 on a 4.25 gap against 60 on 4. The art ratio did NOT move (0.712606 against 0.712000), which is what says this is one component redrawn on a rounder gutter. ⛔ The footer prints 1.9800 and 50.0000; both are the frame's placeholders and the build drives the rail's own figures. No browser ran.

STILL OPEN: the 357 floor against this cut's 347 and the 0.0710-vs-0.0667 gap ratio, both stated on 9206-19903, plus ONE THIS ROW ADDS - the row's VERTICAL placement. 123.5 is 15 below a centring of the space above the footer (108.5), and 2 x 123.5 + 60 = 307, so it is exact centring in a 307-tall region that nothing on the board draws. ★ That is the SAME SHAPE as the desktop Auto cuts, where the row sits 18.000 below its centring inside an implied 547 (see 9204-17690): the Auto row is drawn below centre on every cut, by 15 here and 18 there, and no board states either region. Corroborated across two widths and RECORDED, not built - a literal would break the moment the board's height moves, and on the desktop cut the x divergence is proven to be a stale centring of the same kind. The board floor was lifted to 357 in an earlier pass, which covers this 347 without clipping. No browser ran.
